units.en: These localisation keys may unintentionally make the country name be something unexpected. For example, the base game ⟦0⟧ national spirit ⟦1⟧ gets used as the country's name when it gets a leader with the ⟦2⟧ ideology type, making it have the name of "Liberalism". To find such instances, ⟦3⟧. By searching for the country's unintended name surrounded by quotes (in this case, ⟦4⟧) in all of the loaded localisation files (usually the mod and the base game), the file with the root cause can be found to know the localisation key. From this key, every instance of the database entry with the overlapping name can be found and edited with another folder search, with the localisation key either deleted by copying over the entire file if necessary or ⟦5⟧.
most text editors have capacity to search entire folders

Other than the country name, there are certain other aspects of localisation that are commonly used to provide country-specific flair. Same as the name, this can go into any ⟦0⟧ file with the UTF-8-BOM encoding:

Party names. More strictly, parties are country-specific names for ideology group that show up near the pie chart in the politics and diplomacy menus, whose names can also be accessed elsewhere with ⟦0⟧. A party uses up to 2 localisation keys: the regular name that appears in the piechart and the optional long name, which appears when hovering over the party name. If the long name is undefined, it will re-use the regular name.
A localisation key for the regular name follows the ⟦0⟧ format, while the long name uses the ⟦1⟧ format.

Equipment: In order to rename an equipment type for a country, the localisation key used for it needs to be prefixed with the country's tag (separated with an underscore), such as ⟦0⟧. Equipment may also have an optional short name, by appending ⟦1⟧ to the key. Equipment is defined in ⟦2⟧ files, where the IDs can be obtained. The same also works for equipment modules.

If the country will exist at the start, an order of battle is necessary for the country to have an army. Orders of battle are used for establishing the starting military of the country, and they are generally separated into land, naval, and air branches, since enabling the ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ DLCs requires separate definitions for the navy and the air force respectively that are not compatible with the DLC being disabled.

Land units require a template of some sort, which assigns the necessary information. The template definition is equivalent to the ⟦0⟧ effect internally. A simple template can be defined as such:
⟦0⟧ is the name of the division template as it shows up in the template selection. This will also get used for creating or modifying units.

⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ decide the sub-units of the template, meaning ⟦2⟧ and ⟦3⟧ respectively. In particular: subunit = { x = 0 y = 0 } decides the placement of the specified sub-unit. The coordinates represent the Cartesian coordinate system, where (0,0) is the top-left corner, x goes left-to-right, and y goes up-to-down. For a unit to be placed as a support company, it must have group = support in its definition, and to be placed in combat battalions, it must have a different group. The group cannot change in a single y column.

⟦0⟧ decides the placement of the specified sub-unit. The coordinates represent the Cartesian coordinate system, where (0,0) is the top-left corner, x goes left-to-right, and y goes up-to-down. For a unit to be placed as a support company, it must have ⟦1⟧ in its definition, and to be placed in combat battalions, it must have a different group. The group cannot change in a single y column.
By default, the combat battalions have 5 columns and 5 rows, while the support companies have 1 column and 5 rows.[3] The max index is one less than the total amount.

There are other arguments that can be used in a division template, as outlined in ⟦0⟧. The most common one to include is ⟦1⟧: this forcefully changes the name group used for new divisions, defined in ⟦2⟧ files. This is used to automatically generate names and numeration for new divisions, such as a division newly created by the player being named "1st 'Big Red One' Division". If not set, the template automatically picks the name group based on the sub-units.

For the division naming, there are two mutually-exclusive ways to do so:
⟦0⟧ directly changes the name of the division to the given string.

⟦0⟧ instead uses the name group assigned to the division template: is_name_ordered = yes is mandatory to include. name_order = 35 sets the number that gets used for the numeration. If the name group's ordered = { ... } includes this number, that entry gets used. Otherwise, the fallback_name is used.
⟦0⟧ sets the number that gets used for the numeration. If the name group's ⟦1⟧ includes this number, that entry gets used. Otherwise, the ⟦2⟧ is used.

⟦0⟧ is a set of equipment types that the division should use, replacing the default. Each entry in there is ⟦1⟧, which may include: owner = TAG is the owner of the equipment that should be used. This should be the same as the country which gets the order of battle. creator = TAG is the original creator of the equipment that should be used. This is used to determine the variants, and it defaults to the owner if not specified. amount = 14 is how much of the equipment should be there. The rest of required equipment within the archetype will remain ungiven. version_name = "Variant's name" is the name of the equipment variant that should be used. If the equipment type requires a variant to use, such as tanks in No Step Back, this is mandatory. Otherwise, this is optional.
